A note on this quarter

This report covers four months of PR activity (April–July 2026) for Six Senses Residences Comporta and Pinheirinho. The first month focused on brand immersion, press asset development, sales agency alignment and approvals. Since launch, Six Senses Residences Comporta has been nominated for Boutique Hotelier’s Branded Residences Awards and featured in Forbes, Hospitality Interiors, The Observer, L’Officiel USA and 21 further outlets across the US, UK and Europe.

Securing coverage for a pre-construction branded residence is a different discipline from hotel PR: there is no physical product to visit, real-life photography or stay to offer. Coverage has been earned through thousands of targeted pitches and follow-ups, matching the right story to the right journalist, often over multiple conversations and several weeks. Much of this work happens behind the scenes, with active opportunities continuing into Q3 and Q4.

Meanwhile, 29 major Comporta destination stories ran this quarter across Vogue, The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, T Magazine, W Magazine, Town & Country and others. Every relevant journalist behind those stories has been introduced to the project and briefed.

That pipeline creates the foundation for the second half of 2026 and into 2027, as stronger assets become available: clubhouse photography, opportunities to experience Six Senses firsthand and the completion of the first villas. Most media want to cover what is tangible, timely and available. The work now is to keep the project in the right conversations and build familiarity so that when those moments arrive, we’re not starting from zero.

Destination Media Coverage 29 stories · Apr – Sep 2026

Why these stories matter

29 major titles ran Comporta destination stories this quarter, including Vogue, WSJ, Bloomberg, T Magazine, W Magazine, Town & Country, ELLE, The Times, The Independent and Condé Nast Traveller.

Six Senses Residences Comporta does not yet appear in these stories, largely because destination coverage prioritises properties that are open, bookable and available to experience. What this volume does confirm is Comporta’s position as one of the world’s most talked-about luxury destinations, at the exact moment this project is coming to market.

The journalists behind these stories have been briefed on the project. The opportunity now is to convert that awareness into coverage as the story and physical assets develop through the second half of 2026 and into 2027.

Looking ahead Q3 & Q4 priorities
  • 1.
    Golf: go-to-market strategy & Legends Tour communications

    The Pinheirinho golf course is an untold story with strong standalone potential across Golf Digest, Golf Business News and European golf trade media. The first step is alignment with the Golf Director to build the go-to-market communications strategy, covering the course, clubhouse programme, Legends Tour and supporting press assets.

    To take the story to market, we need clarity on membership, public access, the clubhouse F&B concept and overall positioning. Once finalised, this creates a significant trade and consumer news moment independent of the residences.

    Needs: golf programme details, clubhouse completion timeline, meetings with Golf Director and F&B Director
  • 2.
    Clubhouse design feature

    Designed by Jacobsen Architecture, the clubhouse has standalone potential across architecture, interiors and lifestyle media. Real photography is the priority, positioning us to target W Magazine, Wallpaper*, Architectural Digest, Dezeen and others going into 2027.

    Needs: confirmed completion timeline and approved real photography
  • 3.
    Golf destination press trip

    Following Cathy Hawker's FT site visit in July, the next opportunity is a broader golf and destination press trip, ideally in autumn or, if timing requires, spring 2027. Timing depends on the clubhouse being completed, furnished and press-ready. Targets include Architectural Digest, Forbes, Wallpaper* and The Times UK.

    Needs: clubhouse completion and confirmed press-trip window
  • 4.
    Owner case study: Anthony & Soha Encarnacao

    Captured in July, the owner story is now being developed for WSJ, The Times or the Financial Times. Buyer stories are particularly valuable for pre-construction developments, providing a human proof point when the physical product is still taking shape.

    Target: winter placement.

  • 5.
    Standalone Forbes & Robb Report features

    Both opportunities remain active. Forbes requires approved pricing for the top residence and at least 3 to 5 interior renders; the Robb Report exclusive pitch is ready to go subject to the same approvals. These remain two of the highest-impact standalone opportunities available for 2026.

    Needs: price approval and interior render from João / Marcos

Decisions needed from client

1. Approve price of top and lowest residence for Forbes and Robb Report pitching Needed ASAP
2. Confirm golf programme details: membership model, public access, F&B concept, clubhouse positioning — required to develop press release Q4 2026
3. Confirm clubhouse completion timeline so photography can be planned and executed in autumn Q4 2026
4. Connect PR and communications team with golf director for strategic alignment and joint communications plan Q4 2026
